resolution.rationale: Upstream v0.94.0 moves the SDK imports to @agentclientprotocol/sdk/unstable (#1386, ACP SDK 2.0.0), including the RequestError import of src/goal-extension.ts, and adds AIR_LOAD_REPLAY_END_CAPABILITY and AIR_LOAD_REPLAY_END_KEY next to the goal keys in the air-extension import list of src/acp-agent.ts (#1361). Both are context lines of this patch. The v0.91 adaptation c16a02cb2c98479194eab5e833a54f45d4e21a4c still applies to the bare v0.94.0 tag, but its replay gets a different stable patch-id, so the candidate build no longer sees the second copy of it in alas history (2a888894c25f9d342ddb59caa8cde25d5dd5fb99) as already applied and fails replaying it on top of the first. The replacement reapplies the patch on v0.94.0 with the same added and removed lines; only the context differs. Upstream v0.94.0 does not touch goal negotiation, goals stay AIR-only upstream, and the load replay end update is a separate AIR capability that this patch does not gate, so the patch is not absorbed. The replacement has a stable patch-id distinct from every retired commit, and the goal tests pass on it.

resolution.rationale: Upstream v0.94.0 (#1386, ACP SDK 2.0.0) moves the ClientCapabilities import of src/async-tasks.ts to @agentclientprotocol/sdk/unstable, a context line of this patch, and the patch is written on top of the goal opt-in, which is adapted again for v0.94. The candidate replays original downstream commits before adaptation commits, so the v0.91 commit 7f504014fe77d895a99adee24e3ca09d735b4eb8 conflicts. The replacement reapplies it on top of the v0.94 goal adaptation with the same added and removed lines. Upstream async tasks remain AIR-only and clientSupportsAsyncTasks and its callers are unchanged. Upstream #1384 (Claude Code 2.1.303) turns on fork subagents in the Agent SDK; fork children are subagents, not async tasks, and the fork replay fix in subagent-history.ts does not read the async task capability, so an opted-in non-AIR client is still treated exactly like AIR with asyncTasks. The replacement has a stable patch-id distinct from every retired commit; the async task, create-session-options (including the per-task stop affordance cases), tool call contract and native subagent suites pass with it.

resolution.rationale: Upstream v0.94.0 still lists advisor_tool_result among the ignored content blocks of toAcpNotifications, so the patch is not absorbed. The v0.94.0 src/acp-agent.ts edits (the SDK 2.0 import path, the load replay end update and the skill scan cache) do not touch the advisor path. 590b7ed9e90414124c60eb0b853ad6ed4575a24c replays cleanly with an unchanged stable patch-id, and the incomplete-tool suite passes with it.

The patch is written on top of the async task patch: it adds contextUsage inside the asyncTaskCapabilityMeta(...) call of the initialize response and the request next to ASYNC_TASK_CONTROL_METHOD. Both are adapted again for v0.94, so the v0.91 commit 1b1425052d7aa057e3d7ebaf84d1067b7c565a30 conflicts when the candidate replays it before the adaptations. The replacement reapplies the unchanged patch on top of the v0.94 async task adaptation. Upstream v0.94.0 has no _alas/context_usage request or contextUsage advertisement, and Claude Agent SDK 0.3.303 (#1384) keeps Query.getContextUsage({ detail }) and SDKControlGetContextUsageResponse. Upstream #1386 moves the agent to ACP SDK 2.0.0, whose protocol router hands v1 messages to the v1 app, so the replacement adds a test that drives _alas/context_usage from a v1 client through acpProtocolRouter: the client gets the getContextUsage result unchanged, and a bad detail is an invalid params error that does not reach the SDK. The test fails without the request registration, without the params check, and without the advertisement. The test also gives the replacement a stable patch-id distinct from 1b1425052d7aa057e3d7ebaf84d1067b7c565a30, which an unchanged restack would have kept.

resolution.rationale: Upstream v0.94.0 (#1386, ACP SDK 2.0.0) moves the SessionInfo import of src/session-index/session-info.ts to @agentclientprotocol/sdk/unstable, on the line next to the withAirMeta import that this patch removes, so replaying b1b5a7faa341850e4437e887abf78dd6783993c0 conflicts there. It also moves the SDK import of src/session-index/service.ts, a context line of the patch, and the patch is written on top of the goal, async task and context usage patches, which are adapted again for v0.94. The replacement keeps upstream's import path and the patch's removal of withAirMeta, because rows build their metadata with the negotiated key from ./meta.js; the rest of the patch replays unchanged. Upstream v0.94.0 does not change the session index contract and still gates it on AIR's sessionIndex, so the patch is not absorbed. The load replay end update (#1361) is a separate AIR capability that this patch does not expose to clients without the AIR declaration. The replacement has a stable patch-id distinct from every retired commit, and the session index, scenario and prompt suggestion suites pass with it.
